title: GBK-compatible TXT import decodes as UTF-8 and loses Chinese chapters
symptom: Importing a Chinese TXT encoded as GBK without a BOM could silently decode through UTF-8 replacement, turning title, author, and chapter headings into garbled text. A focused import test reproduced the issue by encoding `《编码测试》` and `第1章 开始` as GBK bytes; the import could not find the parsed `第1章 开始` chapter before the fix.
root_cause: TxtCharsetDetector only recognized UTF-8 BOM and UTF-16 BOM markers, then defaulted every other byte stream to UTF-8. Java/Kotlin string decoding replaces malformed UTF-8 by default, so the downstream metadata extractor and chapter parser received corrupted text instead of a clear encoding decision.
fix: Changed TxtCharsetDetector to strictly validate BOM-less UTF-8 before selecting UTF-8.
Fallback to GB18030 when strict UTF-8 decoding reports malformed or unmappable input, covering common GBK/GB2312-compatible Chinese TXT files.
Added detector-level tests for GBK-compatible Chinese bytes and UTF-8 Chinese bytes.
Added an import-level regression that verifies GBK bytes decode before metadata extraction, chapter parsing, charset persistence, and chapter text storage.
failed_attempts: Parser-only external corpus tests are not sufficient evidence for import encoding support because they read already-decoded text and bypass TextContentLoader.
Using normal UTF-8 string construction as a probe is unsafe because malformed bytes can be replaced instead of failing clearly.
impact: Prevents common Chinese TXT files saved in GBK/GB2312-compatible encodings from importing as unreadable garbled text and losing their chapter structure.
